In [[geometry]], the '''5<sub>21</sub> honeycomb''' is a [[Uniform honeycomb|uniform tessellation]] of 8-dimensional Euclidean space. The symbol 5<sub>21</sub> is from [[Coxeter]], named for the length of the 3 branches of its Coxeter-Dynkin diagram.<ref name="coxeter">Coxeter, 1973, Chapter 5: The Kaleidoscope</ref>

By putting spheres at its vertices one obtains the densest-possible packing of spheres in 8 dimensions. This was proven by [[Maryna Viazovska]] in 2016 using the theory of [[Modular form|modular forms]]. Viazovska was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] for this work in 2022.

This honeycomb was first studied by Gosset who called it a ''9-ic semi-regular figure''<ref name="gosset">{{cite journal | last=Gosset | first=Thorold | title = On the regular and semi-regular figures in space of ''n'' dimensions | journal = [[Messenger of Mathematics]] | volume = 29 | pages = 43–48 | year = 1900}}</ref> (Gosset regarded honeycombs in ''n'' dimensions as degenerate ''n''+1 polytopes).

Each vertex of the 5<sub>21</sub> honeycomb is surrounded by 2160 [[8-orthoplex|8-orthoplexes]] and 17280 [[8-simplex|8-simplices]].

The [[vertex figure]] of Gosset's honeycomb is the semiregular [[4 21 polytope|4<sub>21</sub> polytope]]. It is the final figure in the [[Semiregular k 21 polytope|k<sub>21</sub>]] family.

This honeycomb is highly regular in the sense that its symmetry group (the affine <math>{\tilde{E}}_8</math> Weyl group) acts transitively on the [[face (geometry)|''k''-faces]] for ''k'' ≤ 6. All of the ''k''-faces for ''k'' ≤ 7 are simplices.

== Construction ==

It is created by a [[Wythoff construction]] upon a set of 9 [[hyperplane]] mirrors in 8-dimensional space.

The facet information can be extracted from its [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]].
: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}

Removing the node on the end of the 2-length branch leaves the [[8-orthoplex]], 6<sub>11</sub>.
: {{CDD|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}

Removing the node on the end of the 1-length branch leaves the [[8-simplex]].
: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}

The [[vertex figure]] is determined by removing the ringed node and ringing the neighboring node. This makes the [[E8 polytope|4<sub>21</sub> polytope]].
: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}

The [[edge figure]] is determined from the vertex figure by removing the ringed node and ringing the neighboring node. This makes the [[3_21 polytope|3<sub>21</sub> polytope]].
: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}

The [[face figure]] is determined from the edge figure by removing the ringed node and ringing the neighboring node. This makes the [[E6 polytope|2<sub>21</sub> polytope]].
: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1}}

The cell figure is determined from the face figure by removing the ringed node and ringing the neighboring node. This makes the [[demipenteract|1<sub>21</sub> polytope]].
: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea_1}}

== Kissing number ==

Each vertex of this tessellation is the center of a 7-sphere in the densest [[sphere packing|packing]] in 8 dimensions; its [[kissing number]] is 240, represented by the vertices of its [[vertex figure]] [[4 21 polytope|4<sub>21</sub>]].

== E8 lattice ==
<math>{\tilde{E}}_8</math> contains <math>{\tilde{A}}_8</math> as a subgroup of index 5760.<ref>N.W. Johnson: ''Geometries and Transformations'', (2018) 12.5: Euclidean Coxeter groups, p.294</ref> Both <math>{\tilde{E}}_8</math> and <math>{\tilde{A}}_8</math> can be seen as affine extensions of <math>A_8</math> from different nodes: [[File:Affine A8 E8 relations.png]]

<math>{\tilde{E}}_8</math> contains <math>{\tilde{D}}_8</math> as a subgroup of index 270.<ref>Johnson (2011) p.177</ref> Both <math>{\tilde{E}}_8</math> and <math>{\tilde{D}}_8</math> can be seen as affine extensions of <math>D_8</math> from different nodes: [[File:Affine D8 E8 relations.png]]

The [[vertex arrangement]] of 5<sub>21</sub> is called the [[E8 lattice]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.math.rwth-aachen.de/~Gabriele.Nebe/LATTICES/E8.html|title = The Lattice E8}}</ref>

The E8 lattice can also be constructed as a union of the vertices of two [[8-demicube honeycomb]]s (called a D<sub>8</sub><sup>2</sup> or D<sub>8</sub><sup>+</sup> lattice), as well as the union of the vertices of three [[8-simplex honeycomb]]s (called an A<sub>8</sub><sup>3</sup> lattice):<ref>Kaleidoscopes: Selected Writings of H. S. M. Coxeter, Paper 18, "Extreme forms" (1950)</ref>
:{{CDD|nodea_1|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}} = {{CDD|nodes_10ru|split2|node|3|node|3|node|3|node|3|node|split1|nodes}} ∪ {{CDD|nodes|split2|node|3|node|3|node|3|node|3|node|split1|nodes_10lu}} = {{CDD|node_1|split1|nodes|3ab|nodes|3ab|nodes|3ab|branch}} ∪ {{CDD|node|split1|nodes|3ab|nodes|3ab|nodes_10lr|3ab|branch}} ∪ {{CDD|node|split1|nodes|3ab|nodes|3ab|nodes_01lr|3ab|branch}}

== Regular complex honeycomb ==
Using a [[complex number]] coordinate system, it can also be constructed as a <math>\mathbb{C}^4</math> [[regular complex polytope]], given the symbol 3{3}3{3}3{3}3{3}3, and [[Coxeter diagram]] {{CDD|3node_1|3|3node|3|3node|3|3node|3|3node}}. Its elements are in relative proportion as 1 vertex, 80 3-edges, 270 <sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub> faces, 80 <sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub> cells and 1 <sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub> [[Witting polytope]] cells.<ref>Coxeter Regular Convex Polytopes, 12.5 The Witting polytope</ref>

== Related polytopes and honeycombs ==
The 5<sub>21</sub> is seventh in a dimensional series of [[semiregular polytope]]s, identified in 1900 by [[Thorold Gosset]].  Each [[Uniform k21 polytope|member of the sequence]] has the previous member as its [[vertex figure]].  All facets of these polytopes are [[regular polytope]]s, namely [[simplex]]es and [[orthoplex]]es.
{{Gosset_semiregular_polytopes}}
